threads.body: `ProtocolKeyword` did not require `toString()` in the affected Lettuce versions; it required `name()` and `getBytes()`, and valid non-enum implementations can therefore inherit `Object.toString()`. For those custom commands this fallback records a value such as `MyCommand@...` as the operation and query text. Decode the protocol keyword bytes, which are available throughout the Muzzle range, instead.

replies.body:
Addressed in d1a308e666b42f29b5ec24dfddb1e170567bc9ee.

Analysis: `ProtocolKeyword.getBytes()` is available across the supported Lettuce range and contains the Redis command keyword. Decoding those bytes as US-ASCII avoids relying on an optional `toString()` override while remaining compatible with versions that removed `name()`.

Upsides: Custom protocol keywords now produce stable command names, operation attributes, and query text instead of object identity strings.

Downsides: The fallback allocates a decoded string when Lettuce has not supplied the command name.
